title: Emergent heavy fermion and superconductivity near Mott transition in twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Near a bandwidth-tuned Mott transition, the Fermi velocity $v_F$ and quasiparticle residue $Z$ of a metal often vanish. Here, we show that analogous phenomena emerge in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) at integer fillings and can be captured by an emergent heavy-fermion framework within a projective active-band limit. Unlike models incorporating remote bands, our effective heavy-fermion description arises from \textit{mixed-valence Mott} physics via decoupled charge and local-moment sectors. In the charge sector, active bands $c(\mathbf{k})$ hybridize with an emergent \emph{orthogonal fermion} $ψ(\mathbf{k})$ to open a large Mott gap at $|\mathbf{k}| > k_*$ ($k_*$ sets the momentum-patch size) and a quadratic band-touching semimetal near $\mathbf{k}=0$ at neutrality ($ν=0$). The orthogonal fermion is a linear combination of the doublon and holon excitations and may be written as $ψ_i \sim (δn^f_i+\frac{1}{2})^{-1} f_i$. An emergent Kondo coupling $J_K \sim U$ ($U$ is the local Hubbard interaction) between $ψ$ and local moments $ψ'$ frames the Mott transition as a Kondo screening transition, tuned by the twist angle $θ$. Away from the magic angle, a Kondo-screened heavy semimetal develops below $T_K$ (the Kondo temperature) with vanishing $Z$. Introducing anti-Hund's coupling $J_A$ generates an s-wave fully gapped or nematic, nodally gapped superconducting dome near the Mott boundary even at $ν=0$. At other integer fillings $ν= \pm 1, \pm 2$, increasing bandwidth first drives the small-gap Mott state into an intermediate quadratic band-touching semimetal before entering a heavy Fermi liquid with large Fermi surfaces. Our results establish a unified framework for emergent heavy fermion physics with both itinerant carriers and local moments from the $f$ orbital.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive theoretical model to describe emergent heavy fermion physics and superconductivity near the Mott transition in twisted bilayer graphene. By treating the system through an emergent Kondo coupling mechanism involving mixed-valence excitations, the authors predict the formation of a heavy semimetal phase and unconventional superconducting domes at charge neutrality. This establishes a powerful, unified framework for correlated materials research.
main_problem: The research investigates emergent heavy fermion behavior and superconductivity that arise near a Mott transition in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG).
main_result: The authors establish a unified framework showing how mixed-valence physics leads to an emergent Kondo screening transition, resulting in a heavy semimetal phase and unconventional superconductivity.
method: The analysis employs an emergent heavy-fermion framework utilizing an 'ancilla' theory involving orthogonal fermions ($\psi$) to capture mixed-valence Mott states. Techniques include Schrieffer-Wolff elimination, mean-field theory for pairing, and self-consistent determination of excitation weights.

main_assumptions: The theory relies on an emergent heavy-fermion description derived from mixed-valence physics, using approximations like canonical fermions in a mixed state ensemble.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the effective heavy-fermion model using ancilla fermions, deriving the Kondo coupling mechanism from mixed-valence physics, calculating the resulting low-energy semimetal state below $T_K$, and finally incorporating anti-Hund's coupling to predict superconductivity.
why_interesting: The development of a unified framework connecting Mott transitions, heavy fermion behavior, and unconventional superconductivity in a tunable solid-state system like TBG is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated electron physics beyond simple Hubbard models.
